transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I'm here because my family thinks I need to let things go. I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. But I look at data for a living, you know? I'm a computer systems analyst. Actually, I just got put on this new project upgrading our legacy servers, which is a total headache because the previous guy didn't document a single line of his code. Just thousands of lines of absolute spaghetti code. I actually had to buy a new mechanical keyboard just to deal with all the typing—I got the Cherry MX Brown switches, they're the best if you want the tactile feel but don't want to wake up the whole house. My cat absolutely hates the clicking noise, though. She knocked my coffee over yesterday right onto my desk while I was working. 

But, um... what was I saying? Right, the records. When I actually sit down and compare the timestamps, and I look at the missing attachments in those emails, and then I see the way certain community members just suddenly avoid my questions when I bring it up... it’s just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death.
Have you ever heard, seen, or smelled things that others around you seem unable to perceive?

No, I don't... I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, if that's what you mean. My senses are totally normal. Actually, my sense of smell is pretty sharp, though. Like, just last week they changed the HVAC filters in the server room at work, and they put in this new air purifier system that gives off this faint ozone smell. It smells exactly like right before a thunderstorm. 

I tried telling the facilities manager—Dave, he's this guy who insists on wearing Hawaiian shirts year-round, even when it's freezing out—I told him that ozone can actually degrade the plastic casing on some of our older cables over time. He totally ignored me, of course. People always brush you off when you bring up the actual technical specs. It's like talking to a brick wall with him. 

But anyway... no, I don't have any weird visions or phantom smells or anything. I just pay attention to what's actually there, you know? The data.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any medical conditions, or are you currently taking any prescription medications?

No, I don't have any medical issues. I'm not on any prescriptions or anything like that. 

I mean, I guess I take a multivitamin sometimes? But honestly, I usually forget. My sister actually bought me this fancy pill organizer to help me remember, one of those ones with the days of the week printed on it. It's made of this really cheap plastic, though, and the hinges on the little lids are already snapping off after a month. It’s just terrible manufacturing. It reminds me of the casing on those cheap external hard drives our procurement department bought last quarter to save a few bucks. Half of them failed within the first week because the heat dissipation was completely nonexistent. You get what you pay for, you know? I had to spend an entire weekend running data recovery software just to salvage the backup files for the accounting team. 

But, um... yeah. No actual medications or health problems for me. I'm totally healthy.

Do you believe that these people who are hiding the truth about your father's death are also involved in other areas of your life, such as monitoring you at work or trying to influence your daily activities?

No, I don't think so. I haven't noticed anyone following me or tapping my phone or anything crazy like that. It's just the records about my dad that they're lying about. 

Honestly, I don't think they'd even care about my day-to-day life. It's pretty boring, anyway. Mostly I'm just dealing with those server upgrades I mentioned. Actually, speaking of work, they just rolled out this new mandatory training module on cybersecurity, which is hilarious because the platform they're using to host the training is completely unsecure. I ran a quick scan on it during my lunch break and found like three major vulnerabilities right off the bat. I drafted this whole email to the IT director about it, but then I realized he's the one who approved the vendor in the first place, so he probably wouldn't want to hear it. He’s the kind of guy who just wants to check a box and move on, you know? He drives this pristine vintage Corvette to work every day, parks it across two spaces so nobody dings it. I always wonder how much he spends on detailing that thing. 

But yeah, no, nobody is monitoring me at work. They're just covering up what happened with my dad's estate.
